title: Recognition of Environmental Contaminant and Pathogenic Bacteria by Redox Potential Methodology
author: Yakdhane, Tőzsér, et al.

steps.title: Activate bacterial strains
steps.instruction: Inoculate each bacterial strain on Trypto‑Casein Soy Agar (TSA, Biokar, France) and incubate at the strain’s optimal temperature (e.g., 37 °C for the listed strains) for 24 h to obtain a cell concentration of approximately 7 log10 CFU ml⁻¹ (≈10⁶–10⁷ CFU ml⁻¹).

steps.title: Prepare ten‑fold serial dilutions
steps.instruction: From the activated cultures, perform a ten‑fold serial dilution series down to 10⁻⁷. For each dilution, transfer 1 ml into 9 ml of double‑diluted Trypto‑Casein Soy Broth (TSB, Biokar, France) to create the inoculum for redox measurement.

steps.title: Measure redox potential curves
steps.instruction: Place each 10 ml diluted sample into the MicroTester device and record redox potential over time using the Redox software (MicroTest Ltd., Budapest, Hungary). Collect the resulting curves; a total of 165 curves should be obtained for the six bacterial species (E. coli, Salmonella enterica, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Listeria innocua, Listeria ivanovii, Listeria monocytogenes).

steps.title: Fit growth models and extract parameters
steps.instruction: Using R (version 4.2.0) in RStudio (version 2022.02.2, Build 485), fit each redox curve with the Gompertz, Rosso, Logistic, and Rational models. Export the fitted model parameters and first‑order descriptive statistical parameters into a summary table.

steps.title: Perform SVM classification
steps.instruction: In R, apply a Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier with a radial kernel and the default gamma value (γ = 1/number_of_parameters). Use either the fitted Gompertz parameters or the descriptive statistical parameters as input features to classify the bacterial strains.

steps.title: Bootstrap dataset for validation
steps.instruction: Create a larger validation dataset by bootstrapping: randomly sample with replacement from the original parameter table to generate 500 synthetic samples while preserving the original distributional properties.

steps.title: Evaluate classification performance
steps.instruction: Assess the classification accuracy of each model on the bootstrapped dataset. Expected accuracies are: SVM with descriptive parameters = 98.2 %; Gompertz model = 91.6 %; Rosso model = 90 %; Logistic model = 88 %; Rational model = 48.7 %. Note misclassification rates: ~10 % of Listeria monocytogenes and 4.4 % of Listeria ivanovii may be misidentified as Listeria innocua; for the Gompertz model, 47.4 % of L. monocytogenes and 13.1 % of L. ivanovii may be misclassified, etc.
